• Main US indexes decline; Nasdaq off most, down ~0.7%
  • Tech is weakest S&P 500 sector; financials leads gainers
  • Dollar rallies ~0.6%; US crude settles down; bitcoin down ~1.5%; gold off ~2.6%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield jumps to ~4.99%

US EQUITIES CLOSE LOWER WITH INFLATION BOOSTING BETS ON RATE HIKES

Wall Street's three major indexes finished lower with the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC leading declines, off 0.7%, as investors braced themselves for more aggressive tightening from the Federal Reserve after October's consumer inflation report showed that prices are still elevated.

Tuesday's decline in oil prices to two-month lows offered some support. But investors were mostly worried about stubborn inflation and the prospects for higher interest rates with commentary from Fed officials solidifying those concerns.

Traders were last betting on a 9.5% probability that the Fed would raise rates by half a percentage point in December compared with zero bets for this size of a hike before the inflation data, released before market open on Tuesday, according to the latest data from CME Group's FedWatch tool. The odds for a quarter-percentage-point increase in rates rose to 90.5% from 84% on Monday. And lastly traders saw zero chance that the Fed would keep rates where they are (3.75%-4.00% range) after the meeting, down from 16% on Monday.

Fed officials also helped dispel any remaining doubt in investors' minds that the odds for a hike had changed.

Dallas Federal Reserve President Lorie Logan said the US central bank needs to deliver at least two more quarter-percentage-point interest rate increases to bring down inflation, and may need to do so promptly to keep broadening price pressures from getting baked into the economy.

Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid said that inflation is "top of mind" as he signaled support for tightening policy to bring it under control, saying that he didn't think interest rates were restrictive last year, and that he believes "today it's fairly accommodative."

And hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Chris Waller had said that the Fed will need to take more aggressive monetary policy action if inflation continues to move away from its target.

Meanwhile, a report from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Tuesday that the overall level of troubled borrowing in the US economy rose modestly in the third quarter but did not appear to signal a notable deterioration in credit quality.

Still. the indexes did manage to close above their session lows. And while the heavyweight technology sector .SPLRCT fell 1.4% and was the biggest drag on the S&P 500, five of the benchmark's 11 major sectors managed to close higher with financials' .SPSY 0.5% advance leading the charge.

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Vice Chair of Supervision Michele Bowman on Tuesday said she expects inflation to cool next year as long as price pressures from the AI buildout and from the Middle East conflict recede.

"I think first we would have to see those risks being abated before I would be confident in my expectations for next year," Bowman said at the Council on Foreign Relations. "With the status of the labor market the way that it is and conditions as they have stabilized since last fall, I think we should be shifting our focus, or I certainly am shifting my focus, to inflation."

(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Chris Reese)

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 10 nov (Reuters) - El peso mexicano se depreció el martes arrastrado por un avance global del dólar tras la divulgación de datos de inflación estadounidenses mayores a lo esperado, mientras que la bolsa se mantuvo oscilando en torno a su máximo histórico de 72,227 puntos.

El reporte reforzó las apuestas a que la Reserva Federal mantendrá una postura más restrictiva, luego de que autoridades del banco central estadounidense dejaron abierta la posibilidad de elevar, incluso, en medio punto porcentual las tasas de interés en su próxima reunión de diciembre.

* La moneda local MXN= cotizaba en 18.6292 unidades en la recta final de los negocios, con un retroceso de un 0.55%, después de dos jornadas de ganancias.

* "La expectativa de una Fed más restrictiva podría limitar el espacio de Banco de México para continuar normalizando su política monetaria sin comprometer la estabilidad cambiaria", dijo Felipe Barragán, estratega sénior del bróker digital Pepperstone.

* La semana pasada, el banco central mexicano sorprendió con un recorte de 25 puntos base a su tasa clave, a un 6.25%, una decisión cuestionada por analistas ante el deterioro del panorama inflacionario local, la depreciación del peso -que a inicios de septiembre se negociaba por debajo de 17 por dólar- y una economía con un desempeño mejor a lo previsto.

* Una Fed más agresiva reduciría el diferencial entre las tasas de México y Estados Unidos, erosionando aún más el atractivo de las operaciones de carry trade, que durante años han impulsado la demanda de instrumentos locales.

* La bolsa, en cambio, avanzó por sexta jornada consecutiva y terminó muy cerca de su récord máximo, según datos preliminares de cierre.

* El índice accionario líder S&P/BMV IPC .MXX subió un marginal 0.06% a 71,899.12 puntos, luego de revertir sus pérdidas iniciales, impulsada principalmente por firmas del sector aéreo.

* Los títulos de la aerolínea Volaris VOLARA.MX encabezaron las alzas, con un 3.10% más a 15.98 pesos, seguidos por los del grupo aeroportuario GAP GAPB.MX, que sumaron un 2.79% a 449.07 pesos.

* En el mercado de deuda, los rendimientos primarios de los Certificados de la Tesorería (Cetes) cayeron en la subasta semanal de valores gubernamentales, reflejando el reciente recorte de Banco de México.

* La tasa del plazo referencial a 28 días se colocó en 6.20%, 30 puntos base por debajo de su remate previo.

(Reporte de Noé Torres; editado por Adriana Barrera)

(( noe.torres@thomsonreuters.com ;))

Nov. 10 (Axis negocios) -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP), which manages 12 airports in Mexico, has updated its plans for the issuance of the new fiber E that will fund its Master Development Plan (PMD), with a revised amount and date.

The amount the company intends to raise through this vehicle has decreased from 10.2 billion to 8.432 billion pesos, reflecting a 17.3% reduction, according to the latest placement prospectus.

Meanwhile, the new date for the offering execution, originally planned for July, has been moved to November 26, so the new fiber would begin trading the following day.

"This structure allows the group to diversify its funding sources, broaden the base of investors with access to the Mexican airport sector, and optimize capital allocation at the level of concessionary companies, without incorporating a secondary sales component in the offering," the company stated in preliminary documents.

The offer will involve the sale of 400 million investment trust certificates in energy and infrastructure (CBFIs), with an individual price ranging from 20 to 21.08 pesos. At the lowest price, the resources would total 8 billion pesos.

Similarly, the total amount allocated by the fiber to acquire shares in GAP's airports has been adjusted downward by 17.4%; however, it retained the acquisition of a 4.2% stake in each of them.

In this context, the valuation of the airports, which also dropped proportionally, represents 43.5% of the current market capitalization of the airport group.

What did not change was the proportion of total resources the new fiber will dedicate to each terminal, meaning that the Guadalajara Airport, GAP's most important hub, will require just over one-third (36.8%) of the funds from the operation.

Only four properties -- the terminal in the Jalisco capital and the airports of San José del Cabo, Puerto Vallarta, and Tijuana -- will account for 88% of the funds the fiber plans to invest, while the remaining 12% will suffice to acquire shares in the other eight properties.

GAP designed the fiber as part of its financing plans for the PMD 2025-2029, which is the largest in its history and involves an investment of 52 billion pesos (approximately 2.8 billion dollars).

The PMD has already allocated 12 billion pesos in 2025 and will execute another 13 billion in 2026, with plans for the modernization of the terminals in Guadalajara and Puerto Vallarta (which will account for almost half of the total amount), as well as significant investments in Tijuana and Los Cabos (one-third of the funds).

Following the news, shares of the airport operator rose 2.5% during a session in which the S&P/BMV IPC, the most representative market index, was flat near historical highs.

GAP's shares have declined 4% so far in 2026, compared to a 13.8% drop for its competitor Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (Asur) and a 5.2% increase for Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA). During the same period, the S&P/BMV IPC, the main market index, has risen 11.7%.

The airline industry faces a challenging environment, characterized by cautious consumer spending and the impact of rising fuel prices. Some airlines, such as Volaris, have reported particular weakness in the Mexican market.

Banco de México reported that the country's international reserves increased by 150 million dollars during the week ending on November 6, reaching a total of 257,905 million dollars.

This increase represented the largest weekly gain in the last 10 weeks. International reserves are assets managed by the central bank that help address potential external financial shocks and contribute to strengthening the country's economic stability.

Additionally, the total reserves reflected a growth of 2.4% compared to the close of 2025, equivalent to a nominal increase of 6,030 million dollars so far this year.

According to Banxico, the weekly variation was the result of changes in the valuation of the Central Institute's international assets.

Mexico ranked as the sixth country with the highest foreign direct investment (FDI), receiving $34.967 billion during the first half of the year; however, it dropped from fifth place compared to the first semester of 2026.

During the same period, the profits for foreign companies that already had investments in the country reached a historic high of $43.650 billion.

Mexico and Brazil were the only two Latin American countries on the list, which is led by the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, China, and the United States.

The increase in foreign investment was primarily driven by the manufacturing sector and the reinvestment of earnings.

At a press conference following a lunch with business leaders organized by Lide Rio at the Fairmont hotel in Copacabana , in the South Zone of the capital, early Tuesday afternoon (November 10), Douglas Ruas (PL-RJ) discussed the issue regarding a potential second round in the Rio de Janeiro elections.

When asked about his meeting with Minister Cristiano Zanin from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) concerning the action requesting a second round in the state election, Ruas stated:

"I was not a part of any of these actions. The first action requesting the annulment of Garotinho's votes was actually filed by the PSD. They achieved a victory at the TSE. The TSE granted the PSD's request and annulled Garotinho's votes. It is the first time in history that we see someone go to court, win, and then appeal that victory. That is what is happening. I am not part of it; my coalition was not involved. We contested the election, received the vote of confidence on October 4, awaited the decision of the Superior Electoral Court, which announced the results, and the elections of 2026 have already concluded across the entire nation. We are not here to comment on this type of action; we are here working, already discussing and assembling our government team to deliver the best for the state of Rio de Janeiro starting in January 2027."

In closing, Ruas also asserted that "the elections are over. In 2030, we will have another opportunity for those who wish to run, they can be affiliated with a party and seek their registrations with the Electoral Justice."

We are not here to comment on this type of action; we are here working, already discussing and assembling our government team to deliver the best for the state of Rio de Janeiro starting in January 2027."

In closing, Ruas also asserted that "the elections are over. In 2030, we will have another opportunity for those who wish to run, they can be affiliated with a party and seek their registrations with the Electoral Justice."

Inflation in Colombia continues to be relentless, affecting the cost of living in the country.

According to a report recently released by DANE, as of October 2026, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) recorded an annual variation of 6.30% compared to the same period in 2025, when it was 5.51%.

DANE's study confirmed that the categories of Restaurants and Hotels (9.39%), Education (7.44%), Health (7.37%), Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages (7.31%), and Furniture, Household Items, and Ordinary Household Maintenance (6.60%) reported the highest pressures, all above the national average.

Most Significant Increases

Specific products and services that significantly contributed to the annual inflation include potatoes, which saw a price increase of 98%.

Other notable increases were in services related to co-ownership (17.14%), fresh fruits (15.90%), beef (13.31%), urban transportation (10.65%), dining in sit-down restaurants (9.47%), prepared meals outside the home (9.20%), electricity (6.92%), effective rent (5.12%), and rent (5.02%).

So far this year, this indicator increased to 5.94%, which is 1.2 points higher than last year when it was at 4.74%.

Manizales

Manizales, on the other hand, reached a rate of 5.99% over the past year, primarily impacted by Restaurants and Hotels (10.33%), Health (6.88%), and Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages (6.87%).

Nov 10 (Reuters) - The discount on Western Canada Select crude oil to North American benchmark West Texas Intermediate futures CLc1 widened on Tuesday.

WCS for December delivery in Hardisty, Alberta, settled at $25.75 a barrel below the US benchmark WTI, compared with $25 on Monday, according to brokerage CalRock.

  • The discount on heavy Canadian crude has retreated from the blowout levels of earlier this month, in part because global freight rates — while still high — have come down since October, said Rory Johnston, founder of the Commodity Context newsletter.

  • The WCS differential at Hardisty in the first week of November reached as wide as $31 below WTI. At Houston, WCS barrels in late October hit an all-time wide discount of $23 as soaring global freight rates reduced demand for Canadian crude re-exports off the US Gulf Coast.

  • Oil prices eased to a two-month low on Tuesday, after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, easing fears of additional Middle East supply disruptions.

(Reporting by Amanda Stephenson in Calgary; Editing by Leroy Leo)

(( amanda.stephenson@thomsonreuters.com ))

• Los datos del IPC de EEUU refuerzan las expectativas de una subida de tasas de la Fed en diciembre
  • El dólar se fortalece y el oro cae tras conocerse los datos
  • Las acciones de Nvidia vuelven a caer, lo que lastra a Wall Street

Actualizaciones a última hora de la tarde

Por Caroline Valetkevitch y Shashwat Chauhan

10 nov (Reuters) - Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU se dispararon y las acciones de Wall Street cayeron el martes después de que una cifra de inflación estadounidense superior a lo previsto aumentara las posibilidades de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés medio punto porcentual el próximo mes.

El dólar se apreció frente a las principales divisas, mientras que el oro sufrió una fuerte caída.

El índice de precios al consumo (IPC) de EEUU subió un 0,4 % en octubre, una cifra superior a la esperada (link), tras registrar un avance del 0,6 % en septiembre, según datos oficiales. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters habían pronosticado que el IPC subiría un 0,3 % en el mes.

Además, el IPC subyacente (link) —que excluye los precios volátiles de los alimentos y la energía y al que a menudo se denomina «inflación subyacente»— se situó en el 0,3 %, por encima del consenso del 0,2 %.

Las probabilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas (link) medio punto en su reunión de política monetaria de diciembre se dispararon tras conocerse los datos. Antes de que se publicaran los datos, el gobernador de la Fed , Christopher Waller, declaró en Londres que una lectura subyacente del 0,3 % para octubre le llevaría a considerar una subida de medio punto en la reunión de la Fed del 8 al 9 de diciembre.

Lo habitual es que la Fed suba o baje las tasas en incrementos de 25 puntos básicos.

La reciente bajada de los precios del petróleo ha contribuido a aliviar parte de las preocupaciones sobre la inflación que han estado en el punto de mira de los inversionistas desde que estalló, a finales de febrero, la guerra de EEUU e Israel contra Irán (link).

«No es solo el IPC general el que está demasiado alto, sino que la crisis del petróleo se ha filtrado en el IPC subyacente », afirmó Brian Jacobsen, estratega económico jefe de Annex Wealth Management en Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.

«Probablemente, a la Fed le preocupa ahora más la idea de que la IA desplace a otras actividades y empuje al alza los precios. Olvídate del petróleo. La nueva preocupación de la Fed es el coste de contratar fontaneros y electricistas».

El rendimiento de los bonos estadounidenses a dos años US2YT=RR, que suele evolucionar en paralelo a las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subió 18,44 puntos básicos hasta el 4,731 %. El rendimiento de los bonos de referencia estadounidenses a diez años US10YT=RR subió 12,55 puntos básicos hasta el 4,988 %.

Otro factor que lastró a Wall Street fue la fuerte caída, por segundo día consecutivo, de las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O. Los inversionistas se mostraron preocupados por el futuro del director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, en la empresa de semiconductores después de que esta iniciara una investigación interna sobre las acusaciones de espionaje que involucran a la empresaria china Alice Huang.

La caída de Wall Street se produjo tras un fuerte repunte el lunes. Las acciones se habían recuperado de la ola de ventas de la semana pasada , ligada a las preocupaciones por un mayor control normativo sobre la inteligencia artificial a raíz del triunfo demócrata en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU El Nasdaq .IXIC, con gran peso tecnológico, cerró el lunes con una subida del 2,7 %.

Según los datos preliminares de cierre, el S&P 500 .SPX perdió 28,46 puntos, o un 0,38 %, hasta situarse en 7.521,48 puntos, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite .IXIC cedió 185,90 puntos, o un 0,74 %, hasta los 25.067,23. El Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI bajó 161,95 puntos, es decir, un 0,31 %, hasta situarse en 52.227,80.

El índice MSCI, que mide la evolución de las acciones a nivel mundial .MIWD00000PUS, bajó 1,30 puntos, o un 0,12 %, hasta situarse en 1.107,66.

El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 .STOXX subió un 0,3 %.

Los informes de resultados que presentarán esta semana las empresas tecnológicas supondrán otra prueba para los mercados, ya que los inversionistas se muestran preocupados por el coste del desarrollo de la IA y su rentabilidad. Los resultados de CoreWeave CRWV.O, un barómetro de la inquietud de los inversionistas respecto a la IA, se darán a conocer tras el cierre de la sesión.

La espectacular salida a bolsa de Anthropic (link) valoró al creador del chatbot Claude en hasta 1,4 billones de dólares, una cifra ligeramente inferior a algunas expectativas iniciales, lo que supone una prueba para la confianza de Wall Street en el auge de la IA que la propia empresa ayudó a impulsar. La empresa está iniciando la gira de presentación para la venta de acciones.

CAÍDA DEL PETRÓLEO Y DEL ORO; SUBIDA DEL DÓLAR

Los precios del oro cayeron tras los datos de inflación, con el oro al contado XAU= bajando un 2,62 %, hasta los 4.030,56 dólares la onza. Eldólar se apreció.

El índice del dólar =USD, que mide la cotización del dólar frente a una cesta de divisas que incluye el yen y el euro, subió un 0,56 % hasta situarse en 102,25, mientras que el euro EUR= bajó un 0,54 % hasta situarse en 1,1162 dólares. Frente al yen japonés JPY=, el dólar se fortaleció un 0,58 % hasta situarse en 158,81.

Los precios del petróleo cerraron a la baja (link) después de que las autoridades estadounidenses restaran importancia a la necesidad de una acción militar adicional contra Irán, lo que alivió los temores de nuevas interrupciones en el suministro de Oriente Medio.

Los futuros del Brent LCOc1 cayeron 1,08 dólares, o un 1,2 %, hasta situarse en 91,49 dólares el barril. El crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate (WTI) CLc1 bajó 81 céntimos, o un 0,9 %, hasta situarse en 86,04 dólares. Ambos índices de referencia del crudo cerraron por segundo día consecutivo en su nivel más bajo desde el 31 de agosto.

Actualiza valores al cierre

Por Froilan Romero

SANTIAGO, 10 nov (Reuters) - Las principales monedas y bolsas de valores de América Latina cayeron el martes, tras un dato de la inflación estadounidense que estuvo por encima de lo esperado y reforzó las expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Reserva Federal en diciembre.

* El Índice de Precios al Consumidor de Estados Unidos subió un 0,4% el mes pasado, tras un avance del 0,6% en septiembre, informó la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales (BLS) del Departamento de Trabajo. Economistas encuestados por Reuters estimaban que el IPC avanzaría un 0,3% mensual.

* Más temprano, el gobernador de la Fed Christopher Waller había señalado que la entidad debería elevar los costos de financiación a corto plazo el próximo mes, incluso si los datos oficiales muestran que la inflación se moderó el mes pasado, y añadió que se debería considerar una subida mayor, de medio punto porcentual, si empeora el panorama inflacionario.

* Otras autoridades del banco cengtral estadounidense se unierpon al coro el martes en establecer la inflación como su mayor prioridad y dejaron la puerta abierta a alzas de tasas.

* Tras el reporte, el índice dólar =USD, que compara a la divisa estadounidense frente a una canasta de seis importantes monedas, avanzaba más de un 0,5%.

* Las pérdidas fueron lideradas por el peso chileno CLP=CL, CLP=, que cayó un 1,52%, a 985,50/985,80 unidades por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA .MMXIPSAGC, subió un leve 0,07% a 10.597,22 puntos, luego de revertir pérdidas iniciales.

* El real brasileño BRL=, se depreció un 1,46%, a 5,5863 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa .BVSP de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo cedió un 0,57%, a 171.254,97 puntos.

* El peso mexicano MXN= cotizaba cerca del cierre en 18,6185 unidades, con una pérdida del 0,49%. El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 0,18% a 71.987,23 puntos. El lunes tocó un récord máximo de 72.227,22 unidades.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR terminó con caída de un 0,92% a 3.299 unidades por dólar, en su cuarta jornada de bajas; en tanto que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el MSCI COLCAP .COLCAP, caía un 2,13% a 2.521,58 puntos cerca del cierre.

* La economía de Colombia se habría expandido un 1,55% en el tercer trimestre, un crecimiento menor frente al del mismo periodo de 2025, debido al impacto negativo del terremoto de agosto, una moderación del consumo doméstico y algunos choques de oferta, reveló el martes un sondeo de Reuters.

* La moneda peruana, el sol PEN=PDSB, se depreció un 0,12% a 3,4100/3,4130 unidades por dólar. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPEperdió un 1,24% a 1.450,87 puntos.

* Los inversionistas dieron "un sólido respaldo" a Perú en la colocación de bonos sostenibles por 4.500 millones de dólares, la más grande en moneda extranjera de la historia del país, dijo ministro de Economía.

* Los mercados financieros de Argentina permanecían cerrados el martes por la visita al país del papa León XIV.

(Reporte de Froilán Romero. Reporte adicional de Nelson Bocanegra en Bogotá, Noé Torres, en Ciudad de México, Hernán Nessi y Jorge Otaola en Buenos Aires.
Editado por Javier Leira)

(( Froilan.romero@thomsonreuters.com ))

• US CPI data cements December Fed rate hike bets
  • Dollar strengthens and gold falls after data
  • Nvidia stock tumbles again, weighs on Wall Street

Updates to late afternoon

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 10 (Reuters) - US Treasury yields jumped and Wall Street stocks fell on Tuesday after a hotter-than-anticipated US inflation reading boosted chances for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike of half a percentage point next month.

The dollar gained against major currencies, while gold fell sharply.

The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, which was more than expected, after advancing 0.6% in September, according to official data. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3% over the month.

In addition, core CPI — which strips out volatile food and energy prices and is often referred to as "underlying inflation" — landed at 0.3%, higher than the 0.2% consensus.

Odds that the Fed may raise rates half a point at its December policy meeting jumped after the data. Before the data landed, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London that a core reading of 0.3% for October would prompt him to consider a half point hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

The Fed more typically hikes or cuts rates in 25 basis point increments.

Lower oil prices recently have helped ease some of the inflation concerns that have been on investors' radar since the US-Israeli war with Iran erupted at the end of February.

"It’s not just headline CPI that is too high, but the oil shock has seeped into core," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.

"The Fed is probably now more concerned about the idea of AI crowding out other activity and pushing up prices. Forget about oil. The new Fed worry is the cost of hiring plumbers and electricians."

The US 2-year note US2YT=RR yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, rose 18.44 basis points to 4.731%. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes US10YT=RR rose 12.55 basis points to 4.988%.

Also weighing on Wall Street, Nvidia’s NVDA.O stock fell sharply for a second straight day. Investors worried about CEO Jensen Huang's future at the chip company after it initiated an internal probe into spy claims involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

Wall Street's decline followed a sharp rally on Monday. Stocks had bounced back from a selloff last week that was tied to worries about increased AI regulation in the wake of a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections. The tech-heavy Nasdaq .IXIC closed 2.7% higher on Monday.

According to preliminary closing data, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 28.46 points, or 0.38%, to end at 7,521.48 points, while the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC lost 185.90 points, or 0.74%, to 25,067.23. The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI fell 161.95 points, or 0.31%, to 52,227.80.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe .MIWD00000PUS fell 1.30 points, or 0.12%, to 1,107.66.

The pan-European STOXX 600 .STOXX index climbed 0.3%.

Earnings reports due this week from tech companies will be another test for markets as investors fret about the cost of the AI buildout and its profitability. Results from CoreWeave CRWV.O, a barometer of investor anxiety over AI, are due after the closing bell.

Anthropic's blockbuster IPO was seen valuing the Claude chatbot creator at up to $1.4 trillion, slightly short of some earlier expectations, setting up a test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom it helped ignite. The company is kicking off the roadshow for a share sale.

OIL, GOLD FALL; DOLLAR GAINS

Gold prices fell after the inflation data, with spot gold XAU= down 2.62% at $4,030.56 an ounce. The dollar gained.

The dollar index =USD, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.56% to 102.25, with the euro EUR= down 0.54% at $1.1162. Against the Japanese yen JPY=, the dollar strengthened 0.58% to 158.81.

Oil prices ended lower after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, easing fears of additional Middle East supply disruptions.

Brent futures LCOc1 fell $1.08, or 1.2%, to settle at $91.49 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) CLc1 crude fell 81 cents, or 0.9%, to settle at $86.04. Both crude benchmarks closed at their lowest since August 31 for a second day.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by DJ Yap, Lincoln Feast, Peter Graff, Joe Bavier, Jonathan Spicer and David Gregorio)

(( caroline.valetkevitch@thomsonreuters.com ))

Nov 10, 2026

Andina Peru's agricultural exports will pass $15bn this year, Minister of Foreign Trade and Tourism Rogers Valencia said, state news agencyreported on November 9. He also said the country should turn itself into a logistics hub serving South America.

The forecast would keep Peru near the record it set in 2025, when farm shipments reached $15bn, a 17.3% rise on 2024. Growth has slowed sharply this year. Agricultural exports totalled $8.334bn between January and August 2026, up 2.3% from the same eight months of the previous year.

Valencia spoke at a ceremony marking Exporter's Day in Lima. He described the expected result as an achievement but said it was not enough. He added that the Andean and Amazonian regions must be brought further into the agricultural export value chain.

The minister said Peru's export performance had taken a great deal of effort. It rested in part on a constitution that guarantees equal treatment for exporters and for business owners, whether domestic or foreign.

Valencia named bilingualism as one challenge facing the Peruvian workforce. He pointed to China, which he said has 300mn English speakers, and argued that English should be Peru's next step.

He described logistics as another priority. Peru has spent billions of dollars on roads and ports, he said, and must now use that infrastructure to become a logistics hub. Such a role would raise domestic productivity and also serve other South American countries, he added.

The minister said Peru's National Plan to 2040 sets out a national roadmap and a model for growth in the economy. He said this progress came not only from new products and trade agreements but also from a vision covering the whole country. The next task, he added, was to open markets for other products.

Nov 10, 2026

El Economista Peru is set to replace Chile as South America's fourth-largest economy in 2027, based on International Monetary Fund (IMF) projections,reported on November 8.

La Tercera Faster growth in Peru drives the change. The IMF expects Peru to expand more quickly than its southern neighbour every year through 2031, while the two economies are now separated by only a few billion dollars. The estimates come from the fund's World Economic Outlook and were compiled by the Chilean newspaper.

The IMF forecasts Peru's gross domestic product (GDP) at $413.597bn in 2027, a fraction above the $413.443bn projected for Chile. Peru's lead would grow to $435bn against $430.4bn in 2028. By 2031, the IMF sees the Peruvian economy reaching $502bn, compared with $486.5bn for Chile.

The IMF projects Peruvian growth of 3% this year, against 0.6% for Chile. In 2027 the two countries would expand by 2.9% and 2.6% respectively. Peru would grow 3% and Chile 2.3% in 2028. In 2031 the projected rates are 3.2% for Peru and 2.4% for Chile.

Peru's GDP stood at about $342bn in 2025, while Chile's was $357.4bn. For 2026, the IMF puts Chile at $402.2bn and Peru at $399.6bn.

La Tercera reported that Peru could pull ahead even before 2027. The newspaper said Chile's economy shrank by a cumulative 0.4% between January and September 2026. Chile would need to grow 3.6% in the fourth quarter to meet the IMF's full-year forecast of 0.6%.

Brazil would remain the continent's largest economy. The IMF projects its GDP at $2.65tn this year, rising to $3.39tn in 2031. Argentina would rank second, at an estimated $768.206bn this year and $855.399bn by 2031.

Colombia would stay in third place, with GDP of $572.375bn in 2026 and a projected $762.67bn in 2031.

Nov 10, 2026

EFE. Chile's annual inflation rate reached 4.5% in October, with fuel costs the main driver, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE), as reported by

Consumer prices rose 0.5% on the month. Of the 13 divisions inChile's truckers split over nationwide stoppage as San Antonio port dispute ends with 8% rate rise the index basket, six made a positive contribution, five a negative one and two had none, INE said.

Transport recorded the sharpest increases: fuel for private vehicles climbed 5.6% and passenger air transport 4.2%. Food and non-alcoholic beverages rose in 13 of 15 categories, led by vegetables, pulses and tubers at 4.6%, followed by bread, cereals, flours and pasta at 0.8%. Clothing and footwear moved the other way, with clothing down 3.9% and footwear down 4.7%.

Diesel, which is key to the country's logistics infrastructure, rose 12.3% over the period and is up 53.3% so far this year, INE data show. At the end of October, diesel increased by about $0.094 (CLP91.5) per litre to $1.59 (CLP1,558). Petrol of 93 and 97 octane rose $0.042 (CLP41.3) to $1.56 (CLP1,527) per litre. Fuel prices have now risen five times in a row since July, following the impact of the US-led war against Iran, and experts expect a sixth increase in the coming days.

The figures land as the government of President José Antonio Kast looks to growth. It secured approval of an economic and tax reform in early August, including corporate tax cuts, which it aims to use to lift growth to 3.5% by the end of its term. The Central Bank of Chile has cut its 2026 growth forecast to a range of 0.25% to 0.75% and warned of persistent 'inflationary risk' after its latest monetary policy meeting.

By comparison, the economy grew 2.5% in 2025 and inflation closed that year at 3.5%, its lowest in five years.

• Alice Huang facilitó envíos de chips de Nvidia por valor de al menos 7.500 millones de dólares a empresas chinas - The Information
  • Microsoft recupera brevemente el segundo puesto entre las empresas más valiosas

Añadir detalles de la rueda de prensa de Donald Trump del lunes en los párrafos 5 y 6, detalles del informe del NYT en los párrafos 7 y 8, y del informe del FT en los párrafos 19 y 20

10 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O ampliaron sus pérdidas el martes, lo que sitúa al gigante de los chips en camino de perder más de 470 000 millones de dólares en valor de mercado en dos sesiones, a medida que aumentaban las preocupaciones por las repercusiones de la relación del director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, con una empresaria china de la que se sospecha que es espía de Pekín.

La relación del director ejecutivo con Alice Huang (link) contribuyó a facilitar el envío de chips de Nvidia por valor de al menos 7.500 millones de dólares a empresas chinas, según informó el martes The Information (link), citando a dos personas que la conocen. Alice Huang y Jensen Huang no tienen parentesco alguno.

El consejo de administración de Nvidia inició una investigación interna el domingo, y sus consejeros independientes anunciaron el martes que habían contratado al exfiscal federal en funciones Joon Kim y al bufete de abogados Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz para dirigir la investigación de la empresa.

Por su parte, el FBI está investigando por separado si Huang, de 63 años, fue objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera (link). Huang ha confesado a sus empleados que fue infiel a su esposa, pero no ha dado detalles sobre la relación.

El presidente Donald Trump declaró el lunes (link) que había hablado con Huang y le había preguntado si sabía que la mujer era, supuestamente, una espía china. Trump afirmó que Huang le había dicho que «no tenía ni la más remota idea» y que creía al director ejecutivo de Nvidia.

Trump también afirmó que no tenía conocimiento de los supuestos vínculos cuando Huang le acompañó a China en mayo.

Sin embargo, el «New York Times» informó el martes de que el secretario de Estado y asesor de seguridad nacional, Marco Rubio, había informado a Trump a bordo del Air Force One, de camino a China, sobre datos de los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses que indicaban que Huang mantenía una relación con una mujer de la que se creía que era una espía china.

Según el NYT , que citaba a personas con conocimiento del asunto, esta reunión informativa supuso al menos la segunda vez en siete meses que se informaba a Trump sobre esos datos de inteligencia.

Las acusaciones han intensificado el escrutinio sobre la gobernanza de Nvidia, el cumplimiento de las normas de control de exportaciones y la dependencia del liderazgo de Huang (link), lo que se suma a la inquietud de los inversionistas sobre si el gasto masivo en infraestructura de inteligencia artificial generará una rentabilidad adecuada.

Las acciones de Nvidia cayeron más de un 6 % tras un descenso del 4,3 % el lunes, lo que permitió a Microsoft MSFT.O superar brevemente a la empresa líder en IA como la segunda empresa más valiosa del mundo por primera vez desde junio de 2025.

«El debate en torno a la inversión gira en torno a si esto sigue siendo un asunto específico de la empresa o si desencadenará restricciones y trastornos en toda la infraestructura de IA», escribieron los analistas de Bank of America en una nota. «No equipararíamos las acusaciones con un perjuicio empresarial demostrado».

Alice Huang, también conocida como Huang Le, junto con su marido y su hermana, creó una red de empresas en China y Singapur para adquirir chips de Nvidia, según informó The Information.

En el centro de la red se encontraba Shanghái Century Litong, una empresa con sede en China que consiguió en 2023 la condición de socio preferente en la nube de Nvidia, lo que le otorgaba acceso prioritario a los chips de la empresa, según el informe.

Cuando se estancaron los pedidos de chips de Nvidia sujetos a restricciones de exportación de EEUU, Alice Huang utilizó sus vínculos con Nvidia y sus distribuidores para garantizar el suministro, lo que contribuyó a introducir en China unos 240 000 chips H100, H200 y algunos A100, según el informe.

Century Litong alquilaba capacidad informática y gestionaba centros de datos utilizando chips de Nvidia, incluidos algunos cuya venta a China estaba prohibida. Algunos de estos chips acabaron siendo utilizados por Alibaba 9988.HK, Tencent 0700.HK y pequeños laboratorios chinos de IA, según informó The Information.

Alice Huang también ocupó un cargo ejecutivo en Megaspeed (link), empresa registrada en Singapur, que estaba vinculada a Century Litong y ha sido investigada por las autoridades estadounidenses en relación con los envíos de chips de Nvidia desde el sudeste asiático a China, según el informe.

The Information también informó de que Alice Huang aprovechó su relación con Jensen Huang para reforzar su credibilidad, al tiempo que mantenía su función en la ambigüedad y evitaba dejar rastro documental.

Mientras tanto, el Departamento de Comercio de EEUU está retrasando las medidas para incluir a Megaspeed en la lista negra, según informó el Financial Times, citando a personas familiarizadas con las deliberaciones.

El Departamento de Comercio, que preside el comité gubernamental encargado de supervisar la denominada «lista de entidades» de grupos vinculados a China que supuestamente suponen un riesgo para la seguridad nacional, había solicitado más información sobre algunas de las empresas objeto de estudio, según informó el FT.

No estaba claro si Megaspeed se encontraba entre esas empresas, pero el retraso ha hecho que quede fuera de la lista, según el informe.

Ni el Departamento de Comercio de EEUU ni Nvidia respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios de Reuters. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed y Shanghái Century Litong no estuvieron disponibles de inmediato para hacer declaraciones fuera del horario laboral habitual. Reuters no pudo verificar de forma independiente estasinformaciones.

• Alice Huang facilitated at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms - The Information
  • Microsoft briefly retakes the second-most valuable company spot

Add details from Donald Trump's briefing on Monday in paragraphs 5,6, details from NYT report in paragraphs 7,8 and the FT report in paragraphs 19,20

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Nvidia NVDA.O shares extended losses on Tuesday, putting the chip giant on track to shed more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions as concerns mounted over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

The CEO's relationship with Alice Huang helped facilitate shipments of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing two people who know her. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related.

Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation on Sunday, and its independent directors on Tuesday said they had retained former acting US Attorney Joon Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the company's investigation.

The FBI is separately examining whether the 63-year-old Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife but provided no details about the relationship.

President Donald Trump said on Monday he had spoken with Huang and asked whether he knew the woman was allegedly a Chinese spy. Trump said Huang told him he had "absolutely no idea" and that he believed the Nvidia CEO.

Trump also said he had not known about the alleged ties when Huang accompanied him to China in May.

However, the New York Times reported on Tuesday that Secretary of State and national security adviser Marco Rubio had briefed Trump aboard Air Force One en route to China about US intelligence indicating Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.

The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the NYT reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The allegations have intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's governance, export-control compliance and reliance on Huang's leadership, adding to investor unease over whether massive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure will deliver adequate returns.

Nvidia's shares fell more than 6% following a 4.3% drop on Monday, allowing Microsoft MSFT.O to briefly overtake the AI bellwether as the world's second-most valuable company for the first time since June 2025.

"The investment debate is whether this remains company-specific or triggers restrictions and disruption across AI infrastructure," Bank of America analysts wrote in a note. "We would not equate allegations with proven business damage."

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information reported.

At the center of the network was Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based company that secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia in 2023, giving it priority access to the company's chips, the report said.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to US export restrictions stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia and its distributors to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report.

Century Litong rented computing capacity and operated data centers using Nvidia chips, including some barred from sale to China. Some of the chips ultimately served Alibaba 9988.HK, Tencent 0700.HK and smaller Chinese AI labs, The Information reported.

Alice Huang also held an executive position at Singapore-registered Megaspeed, which was linked to Century Litong and has been investigated by US authorities over Nvidia chip shipments from Southeast Asia to China, the report said.

The Information also reported that Alice Huang leveraged her relationship with Jensen Huang to bolster her credibility while keeping her role vague and avoiding a paper trail.

Meanwhile, the US commerce department is delaying efforts to blacklist Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the deliberations.

The Commerce Department, which chairs the government panel overseeing a so-called entity list of groups connected to China that allegedly posed national security risks, had sought more information about some companies under consideration, the FT reported.

It was unclear whether Megaspeed was among those companies, but the delay has left it off the list, according to the report.

The US Department of Commerce and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed and Shanghai Century Litong were not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, and Steve Holland and Humeyra Pamuk in Washington; Editing by Anil D'Silva and Leroy Leo)

(( Anhata.Rooprai@thomsonreuters.com ))

Por Noel Randewich y Chuck Mikolajczak

NUEVA YORK, 10 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones tecnológicas volvieron a cerrar en rojo este martes, ya que los pasos de Anthropic hacia una gran salida a bolsa no lograron calmar la inquietud generalizada sobre la salud del sector de la inteligencia artificial.

Las ventas se vieron impulsadas por un informe sobre la inflación en EEUU que apuntaba a cifras elevadas (link), lo que aumentó las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal vuelva a subir las tasas de interés el próximo mes, junto con la noticia de que Nvidia NVDA.O ha contratado a abogados para llevar a cabo una investigación interna (link) relacionada con su director ejecutivo y el hecho de que el desarrollo de un centro de datos en Ohio (link) se está complicando cada vez más.

Muchos inversores se mantuvieron optimistas sobre las perspectivas de las inversiones en IA, aunque reconocieron que la volatilidad se ha convertido en una realidad del mercado este otoño. El índice Nasdaq Composite .IXIC bajó un 1 % el martes por la tarde. Durante el último mes, el índice ha caído un 1 % o más en ocho ocasiones y ha subido un 1 % o más en seis ocasiones.

«Existe preocupación por lo que ocurre en la cúpula de Nvidia y, si es sustituido, por quién lo sustituirá», afirmó Tim Ghriskey, estratega sénior de carteras de Ingalls & Snyder en Nueva York, quien señaló que considera las ventas en Nvidia y otras grandes empresas de IA como oportunidades de compra. «Pero no veo que Nvidia se vaya a desmoronar. Veo una empresa muy sólida afectada por algo ajeno a su control».

Además de Nvidia, que bajó un 6,5 %, las principales caídas se registraron sobre todo entre las grandes beneficiarias del repunte de la IA que arrasó en los mercados durante las dos primeras terceras partes de este año. El fabricante de servidores Dell Technologies DELL.N bajó un 4,8 % el martes, pero acumula una subida del 161 % en lo que va de año, según datos de LSEG, mientras que la empresa de chips Sandisk SNDK.O bajó un 4,5 % en la jornada y acumula una subida del 257 % en lo que va de año.

Entre las «neoclouds» —pequeñas empresas de infraestructura de IA que han estado bajo presión este mes debido a las preocupaciones sobre su capacidad para recaudar fondos en unas condiciones de mercado más restrictivas—, Iren IREN.O cayó un 10 %, Nebius NBIS.O bajó un 7 % y CoreWeave CRWV.O retrocedió un 3 %. Las tres han caído al menos un 40 % desde que el Nasdaq alcanzara su máximo más reciente el 6 de octubre. CoreWeave tiene previsto publicar sus resultados tras el cierre del martes.

Muchos inversores afirmaron que, en su opinión, la inquietud generalizada del mercado estaba detrás de gran parte de las ventas, a pesar de que fue una jornada repleta de noticias sobre temas relacionados con la IA. El proveedor británico de servicios en la nube Nscale está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar su salida a bolsa, valorada en 35 000 millones de dólares (link), según informó The Telegraph el martes.

Las acciones del fabricante de equipos eléctricos GE Vernova GEV.N cayeron más de un 6 % el martes, después de que la firma de inversión japonesa SoftBank 9984.T revisara sus planes de adquisición de equipos para sus proyectos de centros de datos en EEUU GE Vernova es una de las empresas que participan en el desarrollo de la colosal central eléctrica de gas y el centro de datos de SoftBank en el condado de Pike, Ohio, según indicaron los analistas.

Nvidia NVDA.O estaba a punto de perder más de 470 000 millones de dólares (link) en valor de mercado en dos sesiones, a medida que aumentaba la preocupación por las repercusiones del romance del director ejecutivo Jensen Huang con una empresaria china de la que se sospecha que es espía de Pekín.

Aun así, los inversores se centraban principalmente en la perspectiva a largo plazo.

«Siempre podemos atribuir una razón a por qué las cosas están más volátiles. Y sin duda han estado más volátiles en las últimas semanas, desde octubre, digamos», afirmó Jason Ware, director de inversiones de Albion Financial Group en Salt Lake City, Utah. «Pero, al fin y al cabo, la trayectoria de las acciones en las próximas semanas y meses va a depender realmente de los resultados».

Tras el informe sobre la inflación del martes, muchos inversores centrarán su atención en los próximos grandes acontecimientos para las acciones tecnológicas, que serán la publicación de resultados de Nvidia tras el cierre de la bolsa dentro de una semana y la salida a bolsa de Anthropic en los días posteriores, independientemente de cómo se comporten las acciones en un día concreto.

«Probablemente volveremos a tener beneficios récord el año que viene, a menos que se produzca una recesión o un cambio radical en la inversión en IA, y no espero que ocurra ninguna de las dos cosas», afirmó Ware, cuya empresa tiene en cartera acciones de Nvidia. «Por eso creo que la señal la marcará la trayectoria de los beneficios y un crecimiento económico superior al 2 %. Y el resto no es más que ruido a corto plazo que, como he dicho, se irá disipando con el tiempo».

Las tres han caído al menos un 40 % desde que el Nasdaq alcanzara su máximo más reciente el 6 de octubre. CoreWeave tiene previsto publicar sus resultados tras el cierre del martes.

Muchos inversores afirmaron que, en su opinión, la inquietud generalizada del mercado estaba detrás de gran parte de las ventas, a pesar de que fue una jornada repleta de noticias sobre temas relacionados con la IA. El proveedor británico de servicios en la nube Nscale está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar su salida a bolsa, valorada en 35 000 millones de dólares (link), según informó The Telegraph el martes.

Las acciones del fabricante de equipos eléctricos GE Vernova GEV.N cayeron más de un 6 % el martes, después de que la firma de inversión japonesa SoftBank 9984.T revisara sus planes de adquisición de equipos para sus proyectos de centros de datos en EEUU GE Vernova es una de las empresas que participan en el desarrollo de la colosal central eléctrica de gas y el centro de datos de SoftBank en el condado de Pike, Ohio, según indicaron los analistas.

Nvidia NVDA.O estaba a punto de perder más de 470 000 millones de dólares (link) en valor de mercado en dos sesiones, a medida que aumentaba la preocupación por las repercusiones del romance del director ejecutivo Jensen Huang con una empresaria china de la que se sospecha que es espía de Pekín.

Aun así, los inversores se centraban principalmente en la perspectiva a largo plazo.

«Siempre podemos atribuir una razón a por qué las cosas están más volátiles. Y sin duda han estado más volátiles en las últimas semanas, desde octubre, digamos», afirmó Jason Ware, director de inversiones de Albion Financial Group en Salt Lake City, Utah. «Pero, al fin y al cabo, la trayectoria de las acciones en las próximas semanas y meses va a depender realmente de los resultados».

Tras el informe sobre la inflación del martes, muchos inversores centrarán su atención en los próximos grandes acontecimientos para las acciones tecnológicas, que serán la publicación de resultados de Nvidia tras el cierre de la bolsa dentro de una semana y la salida a bolsa de Anthropic en los días posteriores, independientemente de cómo se comporten las acciones en un día concreto.

«Probablemente volveremos a tener beneficios récord el año que viene, a menos que se produzca una recesión o un cambio radical en la inversión en IA, y no espero que ocurra ninguna de las dos cosas», afirmó Ware, cuya empresa tiene en cartera acciones de Nvidia. «Por eso creo que la señal la marcará la trayectoria de los beneficios y un crecimiento económico superior al 2 %. By Noel Randewich and Chuck Mikolajczak

NEW YORK, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Technology shares were in the red again on Tuesday, with Anthropic's steps toward a big IPO failing to calm general anxiety about the health of the AI sector.

Selling was driven by a hot US inflation report that increased expectations the Federal Reserve will raise rates again next month, alongside Nvidia's NVDA.Ohiring lawyers for an internal investigation tied to its CEO and the development of an Ohio data center getting more complicated.

Many investors remained optimistic about the prospects for AI investments while allowing that volatility has become a fact of market life this fall. The Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was off 1% on Tuesday afternoon. Over the past month, the index has dropped by 1% or more eight times and risen by 1% or more six times.

"There is concern about what happens at the top at Nvidia, and if he's replaced, who's he replaced with," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York, who said he sees selling in Nvidia and other major AI firms as buying opportunities. "But I don’t see Nvidia falling apart. I see a very strong company hit by something not of its own making."

Besides Nvidia, down 6.5%, the major decliners were mostly big beneficiaries of the AI rally that swept markets for the first two-thirds of this year. Server maker Dell Technologies DELL.N was down 4.8% on Tuesday but up 161% for the year, according to LSEG data, while chip firm Sandisk SNDK.O was down 4.5% for the day and up 257% for the year.

Among the neoclouds, smaller AI infrastructure firms that have been under pressure this month amid concerns about their capacity to raise funds under tighter market conditions, Iren IREN.O dropped 10%, Nebius NBIS.O fell 7% and CoreWeave CRWV.O slid 3%. All three have declined by at least 40% since the Nasdaq hit its most recent high on October 6. CoreWeave is due to report earnings after the close on Tuesday.

Many investors said they thought general market anxiety was behind much of the selling, despite a newsy day across AI-related subjects. British cloud services provider Nscale is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, The Telegraph reported on Tuesday.

Shares of power equipment maker GE Vernova GEV.N slid more than 6% on Tuesday, after Japanese investment firm SoftBank 9984.T revised equipment procurement plans for its US data center projects. GE Vernova is among the companies involved in the development of SoftBank's colossal gas-fired power plant and data center in Pike County, Ohio, analysts said.

Nvidia’s NVDA.O was on track to shed more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions as concerns mounted over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Even so, investors were mostly focused on the longer-term picture.

"We can always ascribe a reason as to why things are more volatile. And they have been more volatile the last few weeks for sure, since October, let's call it," said Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group in Salt Lake City, Utah. "But at the end of the day, the path for stocks over the coming weeks and months is going to be really a story of earnings."

Following Tuesday’s inflation report, many investors will be focusing on the next big events for technology stocks, which stand to be Nvidia’s earnings report after the close a week from today and Anthropic’s IPO in the days after, regardless of what stocks do on a given day.

“We're probably gonna have record earnings again next year unless we see a recession or a massive pivoting on AI capex, and I don't expect either one,” said Ware, whose firm owns Nvidia. “And so I think that's going to be the signal is the trajectory of earnings, the economy growing more than 2%. And the rest of this is sort of just short-term noise that will, like I said, get ironed out over time."

(Reporting by Noel Randewich and Chuck Mikolajczak, editing by Colin Barr and Nick Zieminski)

Añade detalles sobre las posibles obligaciones del consejero delegado en virtud del código de conducta de la empresa y actualiza la cotización de las acciones

  • Varios consejeros forman parte del consejo de administración desde la década de los noventa
  • La empresa se compromete a llevar a cabo una investigación exhaustiva
  • Se insta al consejo de administración a recabar asesoramiento jurídico independiente

Por Ross Kerber

10 nov (Reuters) - Las revelaciones de que el director ejecutivo de Nvidia NVDA.O, Jensen Huang, mantuvo una relación extramatrimonial con una empresaria (link), sospechosa de ser una espía china, han obligado al consejo de administración del fabricante de chips a enfrentarse a algo más que una simple conducta indebida por parte de un ejecutivo, lo que plantea cuestiones existenciales para la empresa y dudas sobre la capacidad del consejo para investigar a su director ejecutivo de forma independiente.

Entre los líderes empresariales, «sin duda ha habido escándalos de aventuras amorosas y de acoso sexual. ¿Pero escándalos de “trampas amorosas”? No», afirmó Ann Lipton, profesora de Derecho de la Universidad de Colorado que sigue de cerca los asuntos relacionados con los consejos de administración.

Lipton utilizaba un término que hace referencia a una estratagema de espionaje en la que un agente atrapa a su objetivo fingiendo interés romántico. Entre los ejemplos históricos se encuentra el «caso Profumo» (link) a principios de la década de 1960, y suelen acarrear consecuencias diplomáticas o políticas.

El presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump (link), afirmó el lunes que el FBI está investigando la relación de Huang, un día después de que el consejo de administración de Nvidia iniciara una investigación interna «en relación con las preocupaciones de seguridad nacional planteadas en las noticias (link) », según un correo electrónico que Huang envió a los empleados de Nvidia y que la empresa hizo público.

Hay mucho en juego. Aunque no está claro si Huang infringió el código de conducta de la empresa (link) ni a qué sanciones podría enfrentarse, sus estatutos (link) permiten su destitución «con o sin causa» mediante el voto de la mayoría de los consejeros.

Los semiconductores avanzados de la empresa se encuentran en el centro de una carrera mundial por la supremacía en inteligencia artificial. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China calificó la acusación de espionaje de «acusación infundada, calumnia y difamación».

Huang, cofundador de Nvidia, de 63 años, no tiene un sucesor claro, además de mantener estrechos vínculos con Trump. Huang posee el 3,6 % de las acciones de Nvidia y tiene docenas de subordinados directos, lo que sugiere un control férreo sobre la empresa.

Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O bajaron un 6 % el martes, ampliando así las pérdidas (link) registradas el lunes a raíz de las repercusiones del escándalo de Huang.

LA CREDIBILIDAD DEL CONSEJO

A diferencia de lo que suele ser habitual entre sus competidores, Nvidia opera sin un presidente del consejo entre sus 11 consejeros. Aunque la empresa considera independientes a todos menos a Huang, tres consejeros independientes llevan en el cargo desde la década de los noventa y un cuarto, Mark Stevens, durante la mayor parte de ese tiempo. Solo dos se han incorporado al consejo desde 2021.

Esta lista de miembros, con un carácter casi de club, quizá no resulte tan inusual si se compara con los estándares de los carismáticos fundadores de empresas de Silicon Valley, como Steve Jobs, de Apple, fallecido en 2011.

Pero la investigación estadounidense ha intensificado el escrutinio sobre si los consejeros que han trabajado junto a Huang durante décadas son lo suficientemente independientes como para investigar su conducta.

«Si se trata de una figura como Steve Jobs, creo que tanto en Wall Street como en Silicon Valley se diría que tiene derecho a cierto margen de maniobra o deferencia», afirmó Marc Goldstein, director de investigación en EEUU de la consultora de voto Institutional Shareholder Services.

Esa deferencia podría ahora plantear dudas sobre si el consejo de administración ejerció una supervisión suficiente sobre un director ejecutivo cuyo propio criterio ha sido objeto de escrutinio.

Nvidia declaró el domingo que, aunque su consejo no tiene motivos para creer que se hayan visto comprometidos ni la seguridad nacional de EEUU ni los secretos de Nvidia, su investigación examinaría toda la información disponible (link). El consejo afirmó que tiene confianza en el director ejecutivo y en su equipo directivo.

Goldstein señaló que los miembros del consejo que llevan a cabo esa investigación deberían tener libertad para contratar a sus propios asesores jurídicos con el fin de reforzar su credibilidad. La empresa también podría considerar mantener a los consejeros con más antigüedad al margen de la investigación, añadió Goldstein, para evitar impugnaciones legales por parte de accionistas que aleguen que no fue lo suficientemente independiente.

ASUNTO JURÍDICO

Un factor que deberá tener en cuenta el consejo es si Huang informó a la empresa de la relación. El código de conducta de Nvidia incluye las «relaciones personales» entre los tipos de actividades que pueden generar conflictos de intereses para los empleados, junto con actividades como aceptar trabajos de consultoría externos, ocupar puestos en consejos de administración o desempeñar funciones de asesoramiento.

«Si te ves involucrado en una situación que pudiera suponer un conflicto de intereses, ya sea real o aparente, ponte en contacto con el departamento jurídico de Recursos Humanos para recibir orientación», reza el documento.

Gil Soffer, antiguo funcionario del Departamento de Justicia de EEUU y actual presidente del bufete de abogados Katten, afirmó por correo electrónico que una revelación completa y precisa por parte de Huang sería favorable para su situación actual, ya que «significaría que no ocultó la relación y que, presumiblemente, el consejo tuvo la oportunidad de evaluar la misma, establecer medidas de protección y gestionar de otro modo el posible conflicto».

Soffer señaló que se necesitan más datos públicos para saber si, de hecho, la relación generó un conflicto, si la junta directiva ha actuado adecuadamente hasta ahora o qué sanción, si la hubiera, podría estar justificada para Huang.

En un escenario desfavorable, como que Huang hubiera ocultado la relación y cometido una conducta indebida, «la destitución podría ser adecuada», afirmó Soffer.

Huang percibió 120 millones de dólares en los últimos tres años, según muestra el último informe de representación de la empresa, en su mayor parte a través de concesiones de acciones. El documento afirma: «Nuestros directivos son empleados “a voluntad” y no tenemos acuerdos laborales, de indemnización por despido ni de cambio de control con ellos».

ECONOMÍA POLÍTICA

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, profesor de gestión de la Universidad de Yale, señaló que la empresa se enfrenta a cuestiones adicionales de seguridad nacional debido a los vínculos (link) entre Huang y Trump. Trump, que ha elogiado a Huang, declaró el lunes que había hablado con el director ejecutivo y que creía que «estaría bien».

Estados Unidos ha impuesto restricciones a las exportaciones de chips avanzados de IA a China desde 2022. El año pasado (link) la Administración Trump permitió a Nvidia reanudar determinados envíos a China en virtud de acuerdos por los que el Gobierno estadounidense recibe una parte de las ventas de chips de la empresa en ese país.

Este acuerdo hace que cualquier insinuación de espionaje extranjero resulte más delicada tanto para los ejecutivos como para los funcionarios del Gobierno de EEUU, señaló Sonnenfeld.

«Por eso no conviene que haya acuerdos de capitalismo de Estado. No conviene que el Gobierno de EEUU se involucre tanto en las empresas privadas», afirmó Sonnenfeld.

Adds details on CEO's potential obligations under company code of conduct, updates share price

  • Several directors have been on the board since the 1990s
  • Company vows to conduct a thorough investigation
  • Board is urged to enlist independent legal advice

By Ross Kerber

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Revelations that Nvidia NVDA.O Chief Executive Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company's code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal "with or without cause" by the vote of a majority of directors.

The company's advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI superiority. China's Foreign Ministry called the spying claim "a groundless accusation, slander and a smear."

Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia's stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.

Shares in Nvidia NVDA.O were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang's affair.

BOARD'S CREDIBILITY

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.

The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple's Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.

But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.

"If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street as well as in Silicon Valley would say they're entitled to some leeway or deference," said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.

Such deference could now raise questions about whether the board provided sufficient oversight of a CEO whose own judgment has come under scrutiny.

Nvidia said on Sunday that while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information. The board said it has confidence in the CEO and his leadership team.

Goldstein said board members running that investigation should be given the latitude to hire their own legal advisers to bolster their credibility. The company also might consider keeping long-serving directors away from the probe, Goldstein added, to avoid legal challenges from shareholders claiming it wasn't sufficiently independent.

CALL LEGAL

A factor for the board to consider will be whether Huang reported the affair to the company. Nvidia's code of conduct lists "personal relationships" among the types of activities that may create conflicts of interest for employees, along with activities like taking on outside consulting work, board seats or advisory roles.

"If involved in a situation that could present a perceived or actual conflict of interest, contact Employment Legal for guidance," the document states.

Gil Soffer, a former US Justice Department official and now chair of law firm Katten, said via email a complete and accurate disclosure by Huang would be favorable for his situation now since it "would mean he didn't conceal the relationship, and that the board presumably had the opportunity to evaluate the relationship, set up guardrails and otherwise manage the potential conflict."

Soffer said more public facts are needed to know whether a conflict was in fact created by the relationship, whether the board acted appropriately so far, or what if any punishment of Huang might be justified.

In a bad scenario such as Huang concealing the relationship and engaging in misconduct, "removal could be appropriate," Soffer said.

Huang was paid $120 million over the past three years, the company's latest proxy shows, largely through stock awards. The document states, "Our executive officers are 'at-will' employees and we do not have employment, severance or change-in-control agreements with our executive officers."

POLITICAL ECONOMY

Yale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump. Trump, who has praised Huang, said on Monday that he had spoken to the CEO and thought he would "be in good shape."

The United States has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since 2022. Last year the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.

The deal makes any suggestion of foreign espionage more sensitive for both executives and US government officials, Sonnenfeld said.

"That's why you don't want state capitalism arrangements. You don't want the US government to be so involved in private companies," Sonnenfeld said.

(Reporting by Ross Kerber; Editing by Christian Plumb, Will Dunham and Cynthia Osterman)

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

The average price of roasted chicken in Colombia was $43,703 in October, reflecting an annual increase of 6.78%, according to measurements from the Roasted Chicken Index (IPA).

This figure was reported following the National Administrative Department of Statistics (Dane) announcement that the national annual inflation rate stood at 6.30% in the tenth month of the year.

According to the report, five spending categories exceeded the national average in October: recreation and culture (0.44%), housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels (0.30%), health (0.26%), clothing and footwear (0.24%), and finally, restaurants and hotels (0.23%).

The price adjustment for the dish, which cost $40,928 in October 2025, was attributed to the direct impact of utility rates, labor costs, rental fees for commercial spaces, and operational supplies on businesses.

In terms of city pricing, Medellín registered the highest cost in the country, with an average of $52,670 per unit, representing an annual increase of 18.42%. In Villavicencio, the price reached $44,800, while in Bogotá it was $44,520. In contrast, Cali reported an average price of $40,900, and Tunja had the lowest figure at $36,450.

Regarding the cost structure of raw materials, Nicolás Cruz Walteros, a local economic analyst at Corficolombiana, noted that "while an increase in chicken supply was observed, it does not mean that the input is free from cost increases, particularly due to the price fluctuations of feed ingredients such as corn and soy, which are essential for poultry production."

Furthermore, poultry meat as an input showed a monthly negative variation of 0.30% and an annual increase of 3.43%, indicating that the rise in prepared product prices concentrated in restaurant operations.

In this regard, Valentina Guio, head of Macroeconomic Studies at the National Association of Financial Institutions (Anif), stated that "other costs, such as labor, utility services, and rent, have driven prices upward."

Corficolombiana and financial institutions project that food and meals outside the home will continue to face pressure due to climatic factors associated with the El Niño phenomenon and the impact of the minimum wage on the sector's payroll.
